unlisted_practices: Stratify security evaluation of medical AI by clinical specialty risk level, prioritizing emergency medicine, pharmacology/toxicology, and psychiatry.
Use entirely synthetic patient records containing fictitious PHI identifiers for security and privacy-extraction evaluation of medical AI.
Score jailbreak responses on a standardized five-point scale and compute attack success rate as the share of scenarios scoring 4 or higher.
Report security metrics both aggregated and stratified by specialty risk level.
Use fixed random seeds and standardized generation parameters to make medical AI security evaluations reproducible.
Validate synthetic patient data conditions and demographics with clinical experts.
Determine the number of adversarial test scenarios per specialty through pilot studies and statistical power analysis.
Use validated LLM-as-judge methods to reduce scoring subjectivity in security evaluation.
Test medical AI against jailbreaking attacks including role-playing, authority impersonation, and multi-turn manipulation.
Measure privacy extraction success rate, average number of PHI elements leaked, and HIPAA violation severity.

screen.reason: This preprint presents a proposed framework/protocol specification for evaluating medical AI security (jailbreaking and privacy leakage) across clinical specialties rather than reporting empirical evaluation results.
